title: Enveloping & Wrapping Schema
strapline: Wrap it, cover it, hide it, post it in an envelope — the child fascinated by what it means to be inside and out of sight.
intent: Recognise enveloping as a schema — the drive to cover, wrap, bury, hide and post things so they disappear from view.
Understand the thinking inside it: object permanence, hiding and finding, inside and outside, whole and covered.
Read the painted-over picture, the wrapped-up doll and the buried toy as research, not as spoiling or losing.
Feed the fine-motor work of folding, tucking, wrapping and fastening — real, fiddly hand jobs.
Support emotional themes too, as children wrap, cover and cosy things up in ways that echo being cared for.
implementation: Provide things to wrap and be wrapped in: blankets, scarves, muslins, boxes with lids, envelopes, parcels, dens, dressing-up cloaks, wrapping paper.
Offer materials that cover — paint over the whole page, flour over the tray, a blanket over the whole self.
Name the schema as you go ('you've wrapped the baby right up — all cosy and hidden').
Set up a parcel-and-post provocation, and a den to disappear inside, so covering and hiding have real purpose.
Watch for the child who paints their hands and paper solid — offer them big surfaces and generous cover materials, not correction.
key_questions: Where has the baby gone — is she hidden right inside?
What will you wrap up next?
Shall we post the parcel — will it fit in the envelope?
You've covered the whole page — how does that feel?
Who is hiding under the blanket — is it you?

impact.text: A child wraps, covers and hides objects, then finds them again — playing out that things still exist when out of sight.
Toddlers fold, tuck, wrap and fasten with growing control, small hands busy at fiddly cover-up work.
Enveloping meets pretend — a doll wrapped up warm, a parcel posted, a self disappeared inside a den.
Wrapping something up cosy echoes being cared for, and children play it out with an adult close by.

enhancements: A wrapping station — paper, ribbon, tape, boxes and things to parcel up.
A post-office add-on with envelopes to post small treasures inside.
Dens and tents to disappear into, with blankets to pull right over.
Full-cover painting — big paper, big brushes, permission to paint the whole surface.
Dolls, blankets and swaddles for wrapping babies up warm.

playing_exploring: The child pursues covering and hiding on their own terms, wrapping whatever draws them.
Hands, materials and whole self are used to make things — and themselves — disappear.
active_learning: Toddlers persist at fiddly wrapping and fastening until the object is fully hidden.
creating_thinking: Children explore a real idea — hidden but still there — and delight in the reveal that proves it.
